Her name was Abigail . In October 2024, Abigail passed away at the age of 16. She had lived with complex medical needs and disability caused by medical negligence when she was just 18 months old. Despite her challenges, she lived a life full of meaning, inspiring all who knew her with her resilience, faith, and light. Out of her story, OAKonsult Disabilities Outreach was birthed. And now, in her honour, we are building OAK Centre Prime —a place where children like Abigail will receive the love, care, and opportunities they deserve. 🏗️ What Is OAK Centre Prime? OAK Centre Prime will be Nigeria’s first holistic disability support centre , located in Oolo Town, Ogbomoso, Oyo State. It will serve over 1,000 children and young people annually , offering: Inclusive education and therapy Vocational and life skills training Emotional, social, and spiritual support A safe, residential environment for 250 young people A space for families to find hope and healing We’ve already secured 35 acres of land. Phase 1 has begun with the groundbreaking scheduled for April 22, 2025 . Now, we are stepping into Phase 2 —and we need your help. 💛 We’re Raising ₦115 Million (£65,000) To build this dream into reality, we need to raise ₦115 million / £65,000 for Phase 2. Whether due to inaccessible schools, lack of healthcare, or societal stigma, these children are too often excluded from the fundamental rights many take for granted. At OAKonsult, we believe this is not just a social injustice—it’s a spiritual and moral emergency. The Reality in Numbers – 1 in 10 Nigerian children is estimated to live with a disability. – Yet less than 10% of children with disabilities in Nigeria attend school. – Over 90% of children with disabilities face discrimination, abuse, or social isolation. – Most have little or no access to therapy, rehabilitation, or inclusive care. These numbers are more than statistics—they are real children, many of them with untapped gifts, dreams, and potential. But without access to supportive environments, their voices are never heard, and their lives are often written off. The Barriers They Face Children with disabilities in Nigeria often encounter: – Inaccessible schools – Stigma and harmful cultural beliefs – No therapy or support services – Neglected policies and weak implementation For many families, the burden becomes too much. Some are forced to abandon their child’s education or care altogether due to poverty, shame, or burnout. A New Vision: OAK Centre Prime In response to this heartbreaking gap, OAKonsult is building OAK Centre Prime—a purpose-built facility designed to transform the lives of children with disabilities in Nigeria. Located in Oolo Town, Ogbomoso, Oyo State, Oak Centre Prime will: – Accommodate over 250 children and young people with disabilities – Offer education, therapy, and vocational training in one place – Provide family support and counselling – Champion a holistic model: physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual well-being This is not just a building. It’s a movement to rewrite the story of disability in Nigeria. How You Can Help We’ve secured 35 acres of land and broken ground. Now, we are raising ₦115 million (£65,000) to complete Phase 2 of the centre. Let’s build a place where every child is seen, supported, and celebrated. Together, we can build a future of inclusion. Together, we can honour Abigail’s legacy. OAKonsult April 9, 2025 6:43 pm Across Nigeria, millions of children with disabilities are still hidden in the shadows—unseen, unsupported, and unheard. But OAKonsult is changing that narrative. One conversation, one community, and one campaign at a time. In the weeks leading up to the groundbreaking of OAK Centre Prime on April 22 , our team has been actively engaging across Nigeria to spark urgent conversations around disability awareness, inclusion, and equity. Because children with disabilities don’t just need our sympathy—they need our voices, our actions, and our commitment. 🧡 A Wave of Advocacy Across Nigeria From heartfelt interviews to thought-provoking panels and on-the-ground community outreach, OAKonsult has been making waves across both traditional and digital media . Here’s a glimpse into what we’ve been up to: 🔹 Media Appearances: Our founder, Olufunke Adeloye, has been featured on local TV and radio, sharing Abigail’s story and the vision behind OAK Centre Prime. These powerful interviews have reached thousands—many hearing for the first time what life is really like for families raising a child with disabilities in Nigeria. 🔹 Community Dialogues: We’ve hosted gatherings in schools, churches, and community halls, opening safe spaces for parents to share their experiences, for children to be seen, and for entire communities to begin rethinking disability not as a limitation, but as part of the beautiful diversity of life. 🌍 Why This Matters More Than Ever Did you know that over 90% of children with disabilities in Nigeria never attend school ? Or that many are kept hidden due to stigma and fear? OAKonsult’s recent advocacy efforts aren’t just about awareness. They’re about breaking generational cycles of silence and neglect—and paving the way for real change . Change that starts with the groundbreaking of OAK Centre Prime , a facility designed to serve, educate, and empower children with disabilities with love, dignity, and purpose. 🏗️ A Legacy in the Making: Oak Centre Prime On April 22, 2025 , we break ground on 35 acres of possibility in Ogbomoso, Oyo State. OAK Centre Prime will be: A sanctuary for children and young people with disabilities A hub for therapy, inclusive education, and vocational training A model for holistic, faith-informed disability support in Nigeria This groundbreaking is more than a construction project. It’s a promise to every child who’s ever been left behind that you are seen, you matter, and you belong . 💬 How You Can Be Part of the Movement 🟡 Attend the Groundbreaking Ceremony 📍 April 22, 2025 | 🕛 12 PM – 2 PM | Oolo Town, Ogbomoso, Oyo State 🟡 Donate to Phase 2 Construction We’re raising ₦115 million / £65,000. Give via: 👉 Stewardship UK 👉 PayPal 👉 Nigeria Bank: Stanbic IBTC | 0053838107 🟡 Spread the Word Repost, share our flyers, and use the hashtag: #OAKCentrePrime #DisabilityIsNotInability 🟡 Partner or Volunteer Do you know an organisation or business that aligns with our vision? Let’s connect! 🙌 Together, We’re Making History Every post. Every prayer. Every naira or pound. It all counts. And it all builds something bigger than us. Let’s build a future where every child—regardless of ability—can live, learn, and thrive. Let’s raise our voices until no child is ever left in the dark again. Let’s build OAK Centre Prime. The outreach served children and young people with disabilities, alongside the parents and carers who support them every day. Event at a glance Date and time 7 April 2026, 9:00am to 4:00pm. Location OAK Centre Prime, Oolo Town, along Oyo/Ogbomoso Expressway, Oriire LGA, Ogbomoso, Oyo State. Who it supported Children and young people with disabilities, ages 0 to 25, and their families. Recorded impact OAKonsult’s January to June 2026 impact highlights record that more than 100 children and young people received free medical care through this outreach work. What happened on the day The outreach created a practical community care setting where families could speak with health workers, receive checks and guidance, and discuss next steps for children and young people who need ongoing support. It was designed to reduce the distance between families and care by bringing support closer to the community. Throughout the day, the team moved between registration, consultation, assessment, parent and carer conversations, medical support and follow-up planning. The event was not only about one appointment. It was about helping families feel seen, listened to and better guided in the care journey. Support provided The medical outreach combined health, disability and family-support work. The support included: Health checks Basic medical checks and consultation for children and young people with disabilities. Developmental assessment Observation and guidance to help families understand support needs more clearly. Physiotherapy and functional support Practical input around movement, function and daily support. Parent and carer guidance Space for parents and carers to ask questions and receive practical direction. Psychosocial support Encouragement and support for families navigating disability and care challenges. Care planning and medical aids assessment Individual conversations about next steps, referrals, aids and follow-up needs. Why this matters For many families, disability support is not one simple need. A child may need health checks, therapy guidance, assistive support, school and community inclusion, and a parent or carer who understands what to do next. OAKonsult’s outreach model recognises that families need dignity, practical care and continuity, not only isolated interventions. The day showed the purpose of OAK Centre Prime: a place where children and young people with disabilities, their families, volunteers and community supporters can access help in a setting built around care, inclusion and belonging. The day in pictures These images show the outreach in action: consultations, support tables, volunteers, health workers, community leaders and the wider team that helped make the day possible. Health workers offered practical checks and guidance during the outreach. Volunteers and health workers supported the day from registration to care delivery. The outreach focused on accessible support for children and young people with disabilities. The team worked from an outdoor outreach station at OAK Centre Prime. The outreach brought care closer to families in a familiar community setting. Community relationships helped make the day possible. OAKonsult volunteers, health workers and supporters served together on the day. The outreach brought together health workers, volunteers and community supporters. What made the day possible Medical outreach only works when the practical details are taken seriously. The day required preparation, safe gathering space, registration, supplies, health-worker involvement, volunteer coordination and careful attention to each family that arrived. OAKonsult is grateful for the people who gave their time, skill and presence to serve children, young people and families through this outreach. Continuing the work This medical outreach is part of OAKonsult’s wider commitment to disability inclusion, family support and practical community care in Nigeria. The goal is to keep building pathways where children and young people with disabilities are supported with dignity, and where parents and carers are not left to carry the journey alone. We are therefore pleased to share the new Bromley SEND Local Offer website . One place to find local SEND information The Bromley SEND Local Offer provides a central hub of information and support for children and young people aged 0 to 25 with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), their families, and the professionals who support them. The new website brings together guidance about education, health and social care services, alongside links to local organisations, activities and practical support. Visitors can explore information for parents and carers, young people and SEND professionals, with topics covering the early years, primary and secondary education, health and wellbeing, understanding a child’s needs and preparing for adulthood. Who it is for: Children and young people aged 0 to 25 with SEND, parents and carers, and professionals supporting families in Bromley. Official Bromley SEND Local Offer website launch graphic supplied by Bromley Council. Our partnership in Bromley Bromley Council is listed among OAKonsult’s UK partners — local and specialist organisations supporting parent carers and families. Sharing this official resource is one practical way we can help families reach current local information and help community organisations signpost people consistently. The Local Offer website was developed with community feedback. It also includes opportunities for residents to have their say and see how feedback is being used. headings.text: Empowering Special Needs Families to Live Abundantly
Your Gift Is More Than Support. It’s Hope Made Real.

In 2010, one family’s world changed forever when a medical error led to their 18‑month‑old daughter’s brain injury. What followed was a decade‑long journey through uncertainty, faith, and fierce love. From hospital rooms to community halls, they discovered not just how to survive—but how to fight for every child like theirs. Their daughter, Abigail, defied every prognosis until her passing in 2024, living out the meaning of her name—“Can God be this great?” Her courage in the face of immense challenges inspired OAKonsult’s very creation. Today, her legacy continues to guide us as we serve families facing disability with compassion, faith, and purpose—so that no one walks this path alone.
We Are a Charity Championing Disability Inclusion

OAKonsult is a charity serving families of children with disabilities across the UK, Nigeria and online. We combine spiritual care with practical programmes to uplift, equip and advocate for true inclusion everywhere and live life abundantly

headings.text: We Are a Charity Championing Disability Inclusion
We see families within the disability community empowered, flourishing, and living the dominion life victoriously as people made in the image of God.

OAKonsult has the mandate to empower Parent Carers and families within the disability community with biblical principles and truths that will enable them to find fulfilment in their journeys and to promote an inclusive culture in diverse settings where these families can flourish.
We believe in the sovereignty of God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit in the affairs of man. We hold on to the promise of ‘life in abundance’ as in John 10:10b.

While our faith shapes our ethos and inspires every programme we run, OAKonsult is not faith‑restrictive. We stand with every parent carer of a child or young person aged 0–25 who lives with additional needs or disabilities—whatever your religion, culture, or background. If you love and care for a child with disabilities, you belong here.

OAKonsult is a charity born from love, loss, and unshakable hope. In 2010, Olufunke Adeloye’s world was rocked when their 18‑month‑old daughter, Abigail, suffered catastrophic brain damage due to a preventable medical error in Nigeria. Faced with grim prognoses, the family uprooted their three young daughters and moved to the UK in search of life‑saving care. For years they navigated hospital corridors, sleepless nights, and the crushing weight of uncertainty—yet Abigail kept defying every warning. With every milestone she achieved, the Adeloyes felt a stirring call: to transform their pain into purpose. In 2014, when Abigail was moved to palliative care, Olufunke asked, “How can no one else face this alone?” From that fierce love sprang OAKonsult Disabilities Outreach—a sanctuary of compassion, training, and practical support for families raising children with special needs. Though Abigail passed into glory in 2024, her legacy of resilience and her name—“Can God be this great?”— live on in every family we serve.

Abigail’s Legacy When medical mismanagement left our daughter Abigail Toyitan ventilator‑dependent at 18 months, our family entered a world of wheelchairs and 24‑hour care. Abigail defied every prognosis until October 2024, when she passed away aged 16. Her courage sparked OAKonsult and now inspires OAK Centre Prime—a 35‑acre center in Oolo Town, Ogbomoso, Oyo State, Nigeria where children with disabilities and their families will finally find integrated care, hope and opportunity. Olufunke Adeloye, Chief Executive Officer What Is OAK Centre Prime? A purpose‑built holistic disability support centre designed to serve over 1,000 children and young people every year and to provide safe residential accommodation for up to 250 residents . On one site families can access: Inclusive education and specialist therapy Vocational & life‑skills training Emotional, social & spiritual support Short‑break (respite) and long‑stay housing Community outreach & inclusion campaigns OUR Purpose Diagnose & Intervene Early – paediatric clinic and therapy suites speed up referrals. Offer Respite & Skill‑building – day‑care, short‑break beds and vocational programs empower families. Model Inclusive Community – adaptive sports, worship and enterprise spaces prove that everyone belongs. Donate Now! Who We Serve Children and young people aged 0‑25 with physical, intellectual or sensory disabilities—together with their siblings and parent‑carers—from Nigeria and the wider West African sub‑region. Our Solutions Medical & rehabilitation services Inclusive education from crèche to vocational college Short‑break and long‑stay residential care Parent‑carer coaching & peer support Faith‑rooted counselling and chaplaincy Community sensitisation, research & advocacy Target Impact Over 1,000 children and young people served annually, alongside thousands of parents, carers, and professionals empowered through training, outreach, and integration initiatives. Residential placement for 250 children and young people with special needs and disabilities at its peak, supported by 700 specialised staff . Economic and social impact through job creation, professional training, and capacity building. Programme Overview Project ME is OAKonsult’s flagship wellbeing and resilience programme for parent-carers of children and young people with additional needs and disabilities in Bromley. Inspired by the From Surviving to Living message, the programme helps parent-carers rebuild identity beyond caregiving, strengthen emotional and mental wellbeing, gain confidence and direction, and connect with others who truly understand. The programme grew from OAKonsult’s Civil Society Roots 3 work, supported by the Mayor of London / GLA, and the wider goal of restoring hope, rebuilding identity and helping families live fully again. Register Your Interest What Project ME Addresses Identity and confidence: life before and after diagnosis, rebuilding self-worth, replacing limiting beliefs and setting achievable goals. Wellbeing and health: emotional wellbeing, rest, movement, nutrition and practical ways to manage stress and burnout. Connection and support: peer relationships, mentoring pathways and community spaces where parent-carers feel seen and understood. Voice and advocacy: parent voice, SEND guidance and confidence to navigate services and resources. Future and community: clarity, direction and routes back into volunteering, learning, work or wider community participation where appropriate. Delivery Format Project ME brought together workshops, training, practical sessions, focus groups and therapeutic wellbeing content for BAME parent-carers in Bromley. Support included community connection, parent voice and advocacy training, peer support and mentoring pathways, faith-sensitive encouragement spaces, and guidance on SEND services and resources. Sessions were free for participants through Civil Society Roots 3 support. Project ME impact notes record improved mental wellbeing, increased confidence and awareness, reduced isolation and stronger resilience among participants. Request support Join Project ME Explore support Turning compassion into action Because every carer’s wellbeing matters. Parent carers often carry unseen pressure while navigating family life, appointments, education, finances and emotional strain. OAKonsult creates warm spaces where carers can pause, be heard, find practical direction and reconnect with hope. Our Christian faith shapes our ethos, but our support is not faith-restrictive. We welcome parent carers of all faiths and none, across cultures and backgrounds. If you love and care for a child or young person with disabilities or additional needs, you belong here. Our approach: safe, inclusive, respectful, family-centred and rooted in dignity. Ages 0–25 Support for parent carers of children and young people with additional needs or disabilities. ✓ Wellbeing and confidence ✓ Peer connection and prayer ✓ Practical signposting What we offer Support that is clear, compassionate and easy to access. ✦ Project ME™ Our parent-carer wellbeing programme covering emotional wellbeing, relationships, career, finance, health and faith. headings.text: We Are a Charity Championing Disability Inclusion
We see families within the disability community empowered, flourishing, and living the dominion life victoriously as people made in the image of God.

OAKonsult has the mandate to empower Parent Carers and families within the disability community with biblical principles and truths that will enable them to find fulfilment in their journeys and to promote an inclusive culture in diverse settings where these families can flourish.
We believe in the sovereignty of God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit in the affairs of man. We hold on to the promise of ‘life in abundance’ as in John 10:10b.

While our faith shapes our ethos and inspires every programme we run, OAKonsult is not faith‑restrictive. We stand with every parent carer of a child or young person aged 0–25 who lives with additional needs or disabilities—whatever your religion, culture, or background. If you love and care for a child with disabilities, you belong here.

OAKonsult is a charity born from love, loss, and unshakable hope. In 2010, Olufunke Adeloye’s world was rocked when their 18‑month‑old daughter, Abigail, suffered catastrophic brain damage due to a preventable medical error in Nigeria. Faced with grim prognoses, the family uprooted their three young daughters and moved to the UK in search of life‑saving care. For years they navigated hospital corridors, sleepless nights, and the crushing weight of uncertainty—yet Abigail kept defying every warning. With every milestone she achieved, the Adeloyes felt a stirring call: to transform their pain into purpose. In 2014, when Abigail was moved to palliative care, Olufunke asked, “How can no one else face this alone?” From that fierce love sprang OAKonsult Disabilities Outreach—a sanctuary of compassion, training, and practical support for families raising children with special needs. Though Abigail passed into glory in 2024, her legacy of resilience and her name—“Can God be this great?”— live on in every family we serve.

Apply now All jobs & opportunities ROLE OVERVIEW Keep the Parent Carer Zumba Wellbeing Group running smoothly. OAKonsult is recruiting a friendly, organised coordinator to welcome participants, manage session administration and support engagement with this funded wellbeing programme. This is a paid role. AT A GLANCE Role details Employment: Paid part-time role Pay: £12.71 per hour Hours: 5 hours per month Location: United Reformed Church, Bromley, with some administration completed remotely SESSION TIMES Monthly schedule Every third Monday of the month, 11:30am–1:00pm. Every third Thursday of the month, 7:15pm–8:45pm. The group offers parent carers a welcoming, non-judgemental place to move, connect and support their wellbeing. WHAT YOU WILL DO Welcome participants and coordinate the details. SESSION COORDINATION Create a warm, reliable experience Welcome participants and help create an inclusive atmosphere. Manage registration, attendance records and new participant sign-ups. Send reminders and follow-up communications. Maintain accurate participant records and contact details. Encourage ongoing participation and engagement. FEEDBACK & COMMUNICATIONS Support learning and outreach Gather participant feedback and wellbeing surveys. Take photos and videos only with appropriate consent for reporting and promotion. Provide the media team with accurate information for existing networks and social channels. Work with the CEO and wider team on the group’s ongoing development. WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR Warm, organised and dependable. ESSENTIAL Skills you will use Good organisational and administrative skills. Basic email, spreadsheet and online-system skills. Good communication and interpersonal skills. Reliability and willingness to work as part of a team. DESIRABLE Experience you can build on Administration, coordination or customer-facing work. Surveys, forms or attendance records. Wellbeing, community engagement or supporting families. Lived experience as a parent carer is welcomed but not required. APPLY Apply for the Zumba Group Coordinator role Use the application form below to provide your contact details, a short cover letter and your CV.
